explain.say: Imagine Death arriving without warning and telling you to set out at once on a journey you cannot come back from. That is how the play Everyman begins. It was printed in English in the early 1500s, and it is related to a Dutch play. The panels follow Everyman's last day.

explain.say: Everyman belongs to one of two kinds of medieval drama. On the left, mystery plays: Bible stories from Creation to Doomsday, staged by town guilds. On the right, morality plays: one human soul, with virtues and vices as characters. Which would you rather watch?

Mystery plays filled whole towns. Follow the chain: on the feast of Corpus Christi, each guild staged one story on a wagon, so the shipwrights built Noah's ark. York's cycle has about forty-eight plays. In the Wakefield Second Shepherds' Play, a thief hides a stolen sheep in a cradle! Why mix comedy with scripture?

explain.say: Back to Everyman, an allegory, where characters are ideas. Look at the sort: Fellowship, Kindred and Goods refuse to go at all. Beauty, Strength and Five Wits leave at the grave. Who would leave you first?

The last panel. Only Good Deeds goes into the grave with him. The point is simple and sharp: what lasts is what you did. In 2015 Carol Ann Duffy's version filled London's National Theatre. Great work. Challenge: write the names of three modern allegorical characters.

faq.q: What is the difference between mystery and morality plays?
faq.a: Mystery plays dramatise Bible stories in long cycles staged by guilds. Morality plays are allegories of one human life, with virtues, vices and Death as characters, like Everyman.
Town craft guilds, called mysteries, each took a play suited to their trade and staged it on a pageant wagon, especially on the feast of Corpus Christi in towns like York and Chester.
Allegory gives abstract ideas human form. In Everyman, Fellowship, Goods, Beauty, Knowledge and Good Deeds are characters, so the plot becomes a lesson about what lasts.

faq.q: Why does only Good Deeds go with Everyman?
faq.a: Because in the play's moral, friends, family, wealth, beauty and strength all stay behind at death. Only the good a person has done goes with them.
asks: Who goes with Everyman to the grave?

faq.q: What is the Second Shepherds’ Play?
faq.a: A comic mystery play from the Wakefield cycle. A thief called Mak steals a sheep and hides it in a cradle as a baby, before the shepherds visit the real nativity.

facts: The York cycle survives in a manuscript with about forty-eight pageants.
Everyman is closely related to the Dutch play Elckerlijc.
Carol Ann Duffy's version of Everyman was staged at the National Theatre in 2015.
